update.method: Group C of #2160 had proposed re-pointing OT-05.16 to M22 because the self-glory words (doxazo G1392, doxa G1391) are M22-tagged. Read outward by guide v2 (#2168), with the passages Rev 18:2-10 and Php 3:17-21: both verses were uncited and carry the inner being now. Rev 18:7 takes up Isa 47:7-9 (no widow; one day). Original checked in verse_lexical: G1392 reflexive in Rev 18:7 (the Mat 5:16 verb), G2836 koilia (Rom 16:18 'appetites'), G5426 phroneo in Php 3:19 and Col 3:2, G1391 in Php 3:19 and 3:21. Woven: 10.15 v3 (It gives itself the glory; It tells itself that loss will not come; The boast: In shame; Where it ends: A like measure), Ch 4 v22 (About myself), 10.6 v28 (served as a god), 10.7 v34 (the set mind, beside Rom 8:6; moved from the proposal's 10.4, which has no account of the set mind), Ch 11 v39 (section 4 Glory), 10.10 v35 (another's pride wept over). Rule 77 reconciliation for pride in the touched 10.15 sections: C-214 to C-221, C-228 to C-232, C-235 to C-237, C-182, C-243, C-244 read; none rests on these verses and none needs restating.

new.text: Pride's heart tells itself it will not be moved and that loss and mourning will not come, and it does not lay its end to heart
new.beyond_text: reads Rev 18:7-8 as taking up Isa 47:7-9 and joins the two heart-sayings

new.text: The great city gives herself the glory that the same verb elsewhere gives to God
new.beyond_text: compares doxazo in Rev 18:7 (reflexive) with Mat 5:16

new.text: What comes to the self-glorifying city is in like measure to her self-glory and luxury: the mourning she said she would never see
new.beyond_text: joins the measure clause of Rev 18:7 to the heart-saying in the same verse and to 18:6

new.text: Glorying in shame does the boast's work turned upside down; against it stand the citizenship in heaven and the glorious body to come
new.beyond_text: reads doxa in Php 3:19 as a boast and sets it against doxa in 3:21

new.text: Appetite can be set in the place of God and served

new.text: The mind can be set downward, on earthly things, and the call is to set it on things above
new.beyond_text: joins phroneo in Php 3:19 and Col 3:2 and the noun in Rom 8:6

new.text: Another's pride can be wept over, and the tears go with the telling, not in place of it
new.beyond_text: joins Jer 13:17 and Php 3:17-19 as weeping over another's pride
